content.text:
I submitted index 9 (Sb fraction 0.349) as the best composition. Its measured EQE was 0.125%, the highest of the five I measured. I used all 5 EQE measurements and 4 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.219 | 0.021 |
| **9** | **0.349** | **0.125** |
| 14 | 0.516 | 0.093 |
| 19 | 0.661 | 0.0086 |
| 23 | 0.768 | 0.0035 |

- **The peak is between Sb 0.22 and 0.52.** EQE rises steadily from the Sb-rich end toward the middle, then falls sharply at 0.219.
- **The NiSb₂O₆ ratio (Sb ≈ 0.67) did not give the peak.** I started there because I expected the best EQE near that composition, but it measured about 15 times lower than index 9.
- **XRD didn't explain the peak.** Indexes 4, 9 and 12 (Sb 0.22–0.45) show the same rutile-type pattern. A small NiO peak appears only at index 0 (Sb 0.14). So the drop at index 4 isn't due to a phase change I could see.

**Risk:** I didn't measure indexes 5–8 or 10–13, so the true best could be a neighbour of index 9. With the last measurement I tested index 4, on the theory that EQE kept rising toward the Ni-rich end until NiO appeared. It came out much lower, and that measurement would probably have scored better on index 7 or 11. The score depends on how far 0.125% is below the line's actual maximum.
